t: You're looking at Russell Square, a large garden square in Bloomsbury, almost exactly square, with the British Museum and the main University of London buildings close by. The firm of James Burton built most of it. Over the years several people were born or died on its streets. William Salt, a banker and antiquary, was born here, and the William Salt Library in Stafford was founded in his memory. Thomas Goff Lupton, who died here, engraved many works by Turner. Major-General Basil Davey, who helped plan the bridging for Operation Market Garden, died here too.
